title: Dear Lord, Behold Thy Servants, Here
description: Dear Lord, Behold Thy Servants, Here in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Hosea Ballou wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 725 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “At an Annual Convention”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Dear Lord, be-hold thy ser-vants, here, From var-ious parts to-ge-ther meet, To tell their la-bors through the year, And lay the har-vest at thy feet.

lines: Dear Lord, behold thy servants, here,
To tell their labors through the year,
And lay the harvest at thy feet.
The reapers cry, "Thy fields are white,
All ready to be gathered in,
And harvests wave in changing light,
Far as the eye can trace the scene."
Lord, bless us while we here remain;
With holy love our bosoms fill;
O may thy doctrine drop like rain,
And like the silent dew distil.
While we attend thy churches' care
O grant us wisdom from above;
With prudent thought and humble prayer,
May we fulfil the works of love.

licence: Public domain: Hosea Ballou died in 1852.
credits: Words by Hosea Ballou (1771–1852), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
